note: types/time_unit.rs has no Rust unit tests; the cases pin its documented behavior: a literal unit outside the vocabulary at the operator's unit position (time/add, subtract, diff, isSame at argument 3, startOf and endOf at argument 2), found through guards, effects, tick effects, objects (a render-ui prop) and lambda bodies, while an absent optional unit, and other operators are left alone. A binding string (`@entity.unit`) is a string literal to the compiler and is reported (parity with the Rust check, whose doc comment says a computed unit is left to the evaluator). Operator shapes are the std-time rows of canonical-operators.json fed as SHAPES_HEARD. Message difference: the compiler prints its fixed vocabulary string `ms|millisecond(s), s|second(s), ...`; the lint lists the accepted literals of the installed table, comma separated.

An unknown unit throws at evaluation time, and inside a read predicate that silently drops every row.
